artists.biography:
Iron Maiden are an English heavy metal band from Leyton in east London, formed in 1975 by bassist and primary songwriter Steve Harris. Since their inception, the band's discography has grown to include a total of thirty-six albums: fifteen studio albums; ten live albums; four EPs; and seven compilations.

Pioneers of the New Wave of British Heavy Metal, Iron Maiden achieved success during the early 1980s. After several line-up changes, the band went on to release a series of U.S. and UK platinum and gold albums, including 1982's The Number of the Beast, 1983's Piece of Mind, 1984's Powerslave, 1985's live release Live After Death, 1986's Somewhere in Time and 1988's Seventh Son of a Seventh Son. Since the return of lead vocalist Bruce Dickinson and guitarist Adrian Smith in 1999, the band have undergone a resurgence in popularity, with their latest studio offering, The Final Frontier, peaking at No. 1 in 28 different countries and receiving widespread critical acclaim.

Considered one of the most successful heavy metal bands in history, Iron Maiden have reportedly sold over 85 million records worldwide with little radio or television support. The band won the Ivor Novello Award for international achievement in 2002, and were also inducted into the Hollywood RockWalk in Sunset Boulevard, Los Angeles, California during their United States tour in 2005. As of August 2011, the band have played almost 2000 live shows throughout their career.

For the past 30 years, the band have been supported by their famous mascot, "Eddie", who has appeared on almost all of their album and single covers, as well as in their live shows.

perplexity.description:
Fear of the Dark is Iron Maiden's ninth studio album, released in May 1992 on Parlophone. The record marked a transitional period for the British heavy metal band, arriving as their second album without co-founding guitarist Adrian Smith, who had departed in 1990. Recorded at the Barnyard Studios in Essex, England under the production of Martin Birch and bassist Steve Harris, the album showcases a band searching for creative direction. Opening with the aggressive "Be Quick or Be Dead," the record shifts into slower, blues-influenced territory with tracks like "From Here to Eternity," representing a departure from Maiden's established twin-guitar heroics.

The album achieved significant commercial success, topping the UK Albums Chart and reaching number 12 in the United States. However, its legacy proved uneven. While the title track became an enduring fan favorite and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Metal Performance in 1994, much of the remaining material failed to sustain long-term appeal. Beyond "Fear of the Dark" and "Afraid to Shoot Strangers," few songs entered the band's regular live rotation after 1993, suggesting the album lacked the artistic cohesion of Maiden's earlier work.

The record holds particular significance as the final studio album to feature Bruce Dickinson as lead vocalist. Dickinson departed following the album's tour to pursue a solo career, with Blaze Bayley assuming vocal duties for the next two albums before Dickinson's triumphant return in 2000 for Brave New World. Despite its commercial performance, Fear of the Dark remains viewed as a creative low point in the band's catalogue, overshadowed by both their classic 1980s output and their later renaissance.
